question: F002 surface: subcommand on `python -m jarvis_orchestrate` or new claude/skills/dispatch-plan/ skill?
answer: Subcommand. Operator decision at lock time: the executable primitive should be CLI-first because it works equally well from terminal, Claude Code session, Codex session, future Discord webhook trigger, and any cron / CI. A skill can wrap a CLI; a CLI cannot wrap a skill from outside the agent runtime. Building skill-first would duplicate the dispatch entry surface and bind the new ergonomics to in-CLI sessions. A wrapper skill remains a follow-up if/when in-CLI invocation friction warrants it.
rationale: CLI is the lowest common denominator across all current and planned dispatch triggers. Plan B's Discord trigger will shell this subcommand directly.

question: F002 default behavior: dispatch immediately, dry-run with TTY prompt, or strict dry-run requiring --confirm?
answer: STRICT dry-run requiring --confirm. `dispatch-from-plan <plan-id>` without `--confirm` ALWAYS prints the pre-flight block and exits 0 without dispatching — no TTY prompt, no interactive `y` shortcut, no environment-based escape hatch. `--confirm` is the single, explicit, scriptable affirmative. Rationale (resolves operator review of original D002): the original phrasing offered two confirmation paths (TTY prompt OR --confirm flag) which created two contracts in one subcommand. Operators automating dispatch (Plan B's future Discord trigger, cron, CI) need the deterministic flag; operators using it interactively just type `--confirm` after reading the block. A future `--ask` flag adding interactive `y/N` is recorded as deferred (D006) — additive, never replacing the default.
rationale: One contract, one affirmative. Eliminates 'did I mean to dispatch?' ambiguity. Aligns with bootstrap.sh `--dry-run` precedent and quota-caps init `--overwrite` pattern.

question: What fields go in the pre-flight context block?
answer: TEN fields, printed in this order: (1) resolved plan path (absolute), (2) feature id targeted (default F001 if not specified), (3) tier (from plan.md frontmatter), (4) target_env (from `## Target` markdown section via plan_target.parse_target_section), (5) target_project (from `## Target` section), (6) implementer agent default (plan.agents_required[0] unless --implementer overrides), (7) auditor agent default (plan.agents_required[1] unless --auditor overrides), (8) human_gates declared (comma-separated list), (9) loop_caps.max_iterations, (10) quota readiness label — one of {ok, config_required, calibration_required, unit_mismatch, missing_state}, derived via `circuit_breakers.collect_agent_coverage` (same evaluator the breaker uses, so pre-flight matches post-dispatch); when label==ok, append a `claude=N% / codex=N%` summary line. Original D003 said 'eight fields' but listed ten when expanded; corrected here so contract and field-count match.
rationale: Ten fields covers four 'what is being dispatched' (plan/feature/tier/agents) + three 'where it lands' (target_env/target_project/gates) + one 'how big' (max_iterations) + one 'should I be worried' (quota readiness) + one 'where do target fields live' (path). Fewer hides material context; more buries the lede.

question: What flag set does dispatch-from-plan forward to the underlying volley dispatch?
answer: Five flags: `--feature` (which feature id to dispatch, default F001), `--implementer` (override plan.agents_required[0]), `--auditor` (override plan.agents_required[1]), `--max-iterations` (override loop_caps.max_iterations), `--mode` (interactive|autonomous; P0 still plan-derived only). Excluded: `--volley` (always-on for dispatch-from-plan; single-agent --role mode is operator-explicit and routes through the existing entry, not this wrapper), `--iteration` (single-agent only). Subcommand calls `supervisor.dispatch_volley(...)` IN-PROCESS — same Python interpreter, no subprocess shell-out — so flag forwarding is a function-call kwargs map, not argv reconstruction. Eliminates the original 'shells the volley' wording which was implementation-shape wrong.
rationale: In-process call shares the existing dispatch entry's enforcement (admission gates, breakers, evidence writers) without quoting / argv-reconstruction bugs. Subprocess would buy nothing here.

question: Which quota readiness states block --confirm dispatch?
answer: Four blocking states, all yielding exit 3 with kind-specific remediation: (a) `missing_state` — `~/.jarvis/quota_state.json` absent or unreadable → remediation `python scripts/quota_check.py`. (b) `CONFIG_REQUIRED` — caps file missing OR vendor block missing OR no_cap_for_signal (per F006 evaluator) → remediation `python -m jarvis_orchestrate quota-caps init` (or edit `~/.jarvis/quota_caps.json` if file exists but vendor entry is missing — distinguished by checking caps file presence). (c) `CALIBRATION_REQUIRED` — Claude window with percent_of_plan cap and non-manual confidence → remediation `python -m jarvis_orchestrate calibrate-claude --dashboard-pct N`. (d) `UNIT_MISMATCH` — non-Claude vendor cap.unit ≠ observed_unit → remediation `edit ~/.jarvis/quota_caps.json: unit must match observed_unit`. Dry-run mode prints the readiness label without refusal — operators may legitimately want to inspect the pre-flight before they have ever run quota_check.py. The four states match exactly the BudgetCeilingKind values that mean 'not safe to dispatch' from F006a/b. Stale calibration is NOT blocking (warning-only per D012 of plan 2026-04-30-001).
rationale: Each blocking state has an exact F006 evaluator outcome and an exact one-line remediation. No ambiguity at the dispatch boundary; every refusal points the operator at a specific next command.

question: Future interactive `--ask` flag for y/N prompt mode — defer or never implement?
answer: Defer, additive. If/when operators report friction running `dispatch-from-plan` interactively (vs always typing `--confirm` after reading the block), add an `--ask` flag that prints the block, prompts `Proceed with dispatch? [y/N]`, dispatches on `y`. `--ask` and `--confirm` would be mutually exclusive (argparse group). Default behavior (strict dry-run) would not change — `--ask` is opt-in interactivity. Recording this here so a future reviewer doesn't recover the same UX wish without remembering why D002 chose strict.
rationale: Strict default + opt-in interactive flag preserves automation determinism while leaving room for ergonomic upgrades on demand.

question: F002 quota_readiness=ok semantics: should it cover budget/cap status too, or only config?
answer: F002 readiness intentionally covers ONLY config + calibration + state-presence (the four blocking labels: missing_state, config_required, calibration_required, unit_mismatch). It does NOT cover WindowOutcome.TRIPPED — runtime budget overage is dispatch_volley's responsibility via the F006 budget_ceiling breaker, which fires AFTER admission and uses the same evaluator. Splitting it this way preserves a tight four-state vocabulary at the dispatch-from-plan boundary AND avoids duplicating budget enforcement in two places. BUT this leaves the word 'ok' overloaded: a plan can show readiness=ok at preflight while being over cap, with the breaker tripping after dispatch. Operator review surfaced this as a real semantic gap. Two follow-up options: (a) rename to `quota_config_readiness` so the field name carries the limit; (b) keep the name but print a warning line below the ok label when primary.outcome == TRIPPED ('claude=N% — over cap; will trigger F006 budget_ceiling on dispatch'). Lean (b) — preserves the four-label vocabulary while surfacing the cap warning at preflight time. Deferred to a small CLI follow-up; F002 ships with the gap recorded.

question: Single-agent `--role auditor` agent-name resolution — preserve cross-vendor invariant?
answer: Today single-agent mode (`--role auditor` without `--volley`) dispatches `agents_required[0]` regardless of role, which is `claude` for most plans. This breaks the cross-vendor adversarial invariant the volley mode enforces (claude implements, codex audits — no claude grades a claude). Surfaced concretely during F002 close-out: the auditor-only confirmation round dispatched Claude, not Codex. Fix: when `--role auditor` is passed, default to `agents_required[1]` (auditor slot). Operator can still override via `--implementer` flag (mis-named for this case but already wired). Out of F002 scope; recorded as a Jarvis CLI improvement candidate.

question: Auditor prompt template missing target-context prelude — F023 EC5 self-finding pattern.
answer: Both codex-auditor-i1 (during the volley) and claude-auditor-i2 (during the manual-cleanup confirmation round) produced the same `high` finding: the auditor's OWN summary header did not contain the `Repo: / Env: / Project: / Command:` block that F023 EC5 requires before any logged side-effect commands. The implementer prompt template auto-prepends this; the auditor prompt template does not. Result: every audit pass surfaces the same self-finding regardless of the code under audit. Fix: add the same target-context prelude requirement to the auditor prompt template, so the auditor's own output also conforms to EC5. Out of F002 scope; recorded as a separate auditor-prompt-template fix.
